title: SLO deployment sprint, staffing surge, and dependency 90d slate
body:
Purpose:
Accelerate safe rollout of target SLOs for the model-serving platform while coordinating a temporary staffing surge and clearing high-impact dependencies across infra, runtime, product, and partner integrations. This is a tactical 90-day slate (30/60/90) focused on deployment safety, clear handoffs, and measurable error-budget adoption across services that serve customer traffic.

Scope (what's in/out):
- In scope: definition, canary, and production rollout of SLOs for 6 prioritized service surfaces (API gateway, tokenization, batching router, GPU pool autoscaler, KV cache, and response-streaming). Includes runbook updates, oncall rotations for surge weeks, observability dashboards and alert tuning.
- Out of scope: full company-wide SLO policy (this is a pilot for model-serving surfaces). Long-term platform changes (multi-region replication design) will be tracked as follow-ups.

Desired outcomes (end of 90 days):
- SLOs deployed to prod for prioritized services with canary and rollback hooks.
- Error budget monitoring enabled and integrated with paging/incident routing for each service.
- Staffing surge schedule complete and staffed covers for two 2-week high-risk launch windows.
- Critical dependency backlog reduced: target that 80% of high-severity infra deps have mitigation or cutover plan.
- Acceptance metrics: p95 latency within target for 3/6 surfaces, error budget burn < 30% in first 14 days post-rollout for at least 4/6 surfaces.

Stakeholders and RACI highlights:
- Product-hosted-api: Priya Shah (A) — product owner for API surface and rollout decisions.
- Serving-runtime: Diego Morales (R) — implement routing and kernel config changes for canary variants.
- Observability: Mina Park (R) — dashboards, alerting, log sampling adjustments.
- Platform SRE lead: Ethan Walker (C) — schedule surge staffing and oncall adjustments.
- Exec sponsor: Talia Brooks (I) — high-level progress and approvals for capacity changes.

90-day plan (broken into 30 day tranches):
0-30 days (stabilize & prepare):
- Finalize SLO definitions (latency p50/p95, availability) and test harness via CONFLUENCE-1234. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-05-20.
- Create canary gating policy and rollback criteria; document in repo PR 512. Owner: Diego. Due: 2026-05-24.
- Observability prep: add or update dashboards, ensure low-cardinality metrics for error budget. Owner: Mina. Due: 2026-05-27.
- Staffing surge planning: identify volunteers/rotations and shadowing plan. Owner: Ethan. Due: 2026-05-22.
- Dependency sweep: list blocking infra/partner items, assign JIRA tickets (JIRA-OPS-8742 and children). Owner: Ava. Due: 2026-05-18.

31-60 days (canary & exercise):
- Launch canary traffic for 2 services (API gateway, batching router) to 5–10% of traffic with auto-roll back triggers. Owner: Diego/Priya. Start: 2026-06-01.
- Run tabletop exercises for paging and error-budget exhaustion with oncall rotation participants; record lessons. Owner: Ethan. Target: 2026-06-07.
- Observe metrics and tune thresholds; update alert playbooks. Owner: Mina. Ongoing.
- Clear medium-severity dependencies: complete mitigations for at least 50% of backlog items. Owner: Ava. Target: 2026-06-20.

61-90 days (rollout & harden):
- Roll SLOs to production for remaining prioritized surfaces with staged ramping (per canary policy). Owner: Priya/Diego. Start: 2026-06-25.
- Run two-week staffed coverage windows during rollout peak with documented handoffs and a daily launch sync. Owner: Ethan. Windows: 2026-06-28 to 2026-07-11.
- Post-rollout validation: 14-day burn window monitoring and regression detection (quality metrics + customer impact signals). Owner: Mina. Finish: 2026-07-25.
- Handoff to steady-state SRE rotations and add SLOs to team onboarding checklist. Owner: Ava. Finish: 2026-07-30.

Operational checklists (quick):
- Before canary: confirm runbooks exist, escalation matrix tested, key metric collectors warmed, and canary dashboard green.
- During canary: daily sync (15m), track error budget burn, if burn > 20% in 24h flip canary off and begin rollback.
- After rollout: run incident retro and capture action items in JIRA; mark SLO as "active" in CONFLUENCE-1234.

Communication plan:
- Weekly launch sync (30m) every Monday 10:00 PT in #sre-slo-ramp (Slack).
- Daily 15m during high-risk windows (calendar: SLO-Deployment Daily).
- Exec summary sent on day 0, day 30, and day 90 to Talia Brooks and product heads.

Temporary staffing surge mechanics:
- Surge model: volunteers + short-term contractors (if approved) to provide 24/7 coverage for two 2-week windows.
- Shadowing: 4-day shadow prior to window for any contractor/volunteer new to runtime.
- Reimbursement: Ops overtime policy applies; pre-approved by People Ops.

Key acceptance criteria (must pass to consider SLOs live):
- Alert fidelity: false positive rate < 10% over 7 days on SLO alerts.
- Observability: end-to-end tracing with >80% request coverage for traces of interest.
- Rollback tested: automated rollback works in < 3 minutes in simulated failure tests.
- Documentation: runbooks and handoffs stored under CONFLUENCE-1234 and linked in oncall runbook index.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: upstream partner change (auth/token service) causes sustained error budget burn. Mitigation: circuit-breaker policy + temporary routing to stable variant; escalate to partner on first incident.
- Risk: increased noise in alerts after SLO tuning. Mitigation: deploy alert throttling and add runbook step to mute non-actionable alerts.
- Risk: staffing gaps during surge. Mitigation: pre-commit roster + backup oncall assignment and optional contractor pool.

Dependency register (top items):
- Auth/token service compatibility testing (JIRA-PT-2107).
- GPU pool autoscaler quirk for short-lived jobs (JIRA-INF-3321).
- KV cache eviction tuning required for long-tail workloads (JIRA-RT-1182).
- Observability retention increase purchase (billing approval).

Postmortem and continuous improvement loop:
- All incidents during the 90d slate are to be recorded as postmortems within 48 hours; severity >= P2 must have a remediation plan within 7 days.
- Weekly retro on what changed in the SLO assumptions; create follow-ups for platform product backlog.

Appendix: small templates and quick links (in body for copy):
- Canary gating snippet (example): "if burn_rate_24h > 0.2 or p95_lat_change > 30% then rollback".
- Paging escalation: primary SRE -> SRE lead -> platform eng director -> oncall exec.
- Quick commands: deploy-canary.sh --service=api-gw --percent=5; rollback.sh --service=api-gw

Notes / open questions:
- Do we require legal signoff for increased log retention before observability purchase? Owner: Ava.
- Approval for short-term contractor budget pending finance — aim to confirm by 2026-05-19.

Next actions this week (priority):
- Priya: finalize SLO definitions doc (due 2026-05-20).
- Diego: open canary PR with gating checks (PR 512).
- Mina: create canary dashboard and share for review (due 2026-05-27).
- Ethan: circulate surge roster and confirm volunteers.
- Ava: triage dependency list and attach JIRA tickets.

This doc is intended to be a working slate: expect rapid edits. Keep linked artifacts current and surface blockers early in #sre-slo-ramp.
